1.title: How can I be sure the tools are queried fairly?
1.desc:
Three invariants guarantee fairness in every round.

1. Same context. Both tools receive the exact same question, the same document, and the same timeout. The code that builds the request (backend/tool_arena/rag_tool/ask_one_tool.py) is shared — there is no per-tool special path.

2. Transparent draw. Only tools declared READY at request time enter the draw. They are grouped by task_type (summary, question-answering, extraction); a tool only ever competes with another tool from the same group. Within a group, two tools are picked at random, weighted by a public weight declared in mcp_servers.json.

3. Blind vote. The identities of both tools are hidden until you vote. You see «answer A» and «answer B», never their brand. Any mention of the tool in its own answer is stripped before display.

The code for all three mechanisms is public and auditable: backend/tool_arena/comparison/ask_two_tools_concurrently.py, backend/tool_arena/rag_tool/readiness.py, backend/tool_arena/blind_reveal/hide_tool_identity_before_vote.py.

1.title: What happens when I click «Compare»?
1.desc:
Four ordered steps:

  1. Draw two ready RAGTools (see the fairness question).
  2. Parallel query: the same question and document are sent simultaneously to both tools over MCP. Per-tool timeout of 180s.
  3. Blinding: each answer is sanitized to remove the tool's name, then displayed unlabelled as «answer A» / «answer B». Order is randomised.
  4. Reveal: after your vote, both identities are shown and the vote is persisted.

If one of the two tools errors out, you see an error card in its place and voting is disabled — comparing an answer to a failure is meaningless.

1.title: Why put several RAG tools in competition?
1.desc:
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) is a broad category of tools combining information retrieval with LLM generation. The same label hides very different architecture choices:

  • Which chunker? Paragraph, character window, sentence…
  • Which retriever? Dense (embeddings), sparse (BM25), hybrid, graph-based (LightRAG, GraphRAG)…
  • Which reranker? Cross-encoder, LLM-judge, or none.
  • Which prompt? The same question can yield radically different outputs depending on the prompt that wraps the retrieved passages.

CompaRAG today races five engine families (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack, Txtai, Chroma) on the same LLM (Mistral Medium 3.1 via OpenRouter). The LLM constant is deliberate: we measure the quality of the retrieval pipeline, not the LLM.

1.title: What happens to my question, answer, vote?
1.desc:
Your questions and votes are published as an open dataset on Hugging Face (comparag-tool-votes) after PII filtering. That is the project's purpose: build a public corpus of human preferences between RAG tools, usable to train and evaluate other systems.

Documents you upload are not published. They are passed to both RAG tools so they can answer, then dropped from the cache at the end of the session (24h).

You can request the removal of a specific vote by contacting us — the vote is then archived and excluded from the next dataset export.

1.title: How do I add my own RAG tool to the arena?
1.desc:
The arena is built to grow. Five steps, ~30 minutes:

  1. Copy the template mcp_servers/_template_new_tool/.
  2. Fill tool.manifest.yaml (name, goal, transport, port, task_type).
  3. Implement the rag_query(task, goal, document_content) function in server.py with your tool's logic.
  4. Run python scripts/register_tool.py <slug> — it updates mcp_servers.json and the ontology automatically.
  5. Run pytest backend/ and python scripts/check_openrouter_providers.py.

Full guide: docs/add_a_new_rag_tool.md. Candidate tools to scout: LightRAG, R2R, Vectara MCP, PaperQA2, Verba, RAGFlow, Cohere RAG, Pinecone MCP.

privacy.dataAccessDatasets: Dialogue and preference data are published under an open license on Hugging Face: huggingface.co/datasets/ArthurSrz/comparag-tool-votes.
privacy.dataAccessDesc: The project's code is public on GitHub. No usage statistics are currently published.

privacy.desc: The service is operated by the maintainer of the open-source CompaRAG project.
privacy.dataTimeDesc: Data related to users and their RAG tool comparisons are kept from the moment the preference vote is recorded.
privacy.privacyDataArena: Data related to comparisons: questions asked by users, the answers from both RAG tools, and the user's expressed preference.

1.1: CompaRAG lets users blindly compare several RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) tools on the same question and produces an open dataset of human preferences between these tools. This transparency serves both research (measuring the quality of retrieval pipelines) and the ecosystem (guiding technical choices).
1.4: The project follows eco-design principles for digital services (response cache, lazy corpus indexing, no third-party analytics). The code is public on GitHub: github.com/ArthurSrz/CompaRAG.
1.3: The service is mainly aimed at RAG developers, information-retrieval researchers, product teams who need to choose a RAG pipeline for their application, and trainers who want to explain concrete differences between RAG approaches.

1.1: Simplified user experience: navigation paths are optimised around the essential features of CompaRAG (ask a question, compare two tools blindly, vote, reveal the identities).
1.2: User awareness about the ecological footprint of the service: where available, the energy cost of each RAG tool call is surfaced, and a single shared LLM is used across tools to keep the comparison fair and limit cost.

7.5: Allow the user to interrupt inference (answer loading) during the comparison of two RAG tools.

tos.defsEditor: "Editor" designates the maintainer of the open-source project CompaRAG.
tos.descEditor: CompaRAG is a platform for blindly comparing RAG tools, aimed at the general public, with three goals: (1) measure the real-world quality of RAG tools on user questions, (2) collect human preferences to produce an open dataset, and (3) rank tools according to those preferences.
tos.featuresDatasetsMore: The editor publishes the dialogue and preference data under an open license on Hugging Face: huggingface.co/datasets/ArthurSrz/comparag-tool-votes.
tos.defsModels: "RAG tools" designates the Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipelines compared on the platform — each combines an information-retrieval mechanism with a language model to produce an answer.
tos.descUse: The user asks a question (and optionally uploads a document) and gets answers from two anonymous RAG tools. They vote for the answer that best matches their question. Data is collected throughout in compliance with privacy, and the resulting datasets are published open source.
tos.featuresDesc: To meet the dual goal of informing RAG architecture choices and collecting user preferences, the services offered by the platform without access restrictions are the following:
tos.featuresDescMore: A human-machine interface to send the same question to two RAG tools and vote for the preferred answer.
tos.featuresModels: The RAG tools integrated into the platform are deployed on their own servers or exposed via the MCP protocol. The platform queries them in parallel on the user's question, without revealing their identity before the vote.
tos.featuresModelsMore: A comparison interface for RAG tools.
tos.featuresVote: The user can view the list of RAG tools integrated into the comparator and access their characteristics (framework, architectural choices, performance).
tos.featuresDatasets: The service collects comparison data (questions, answers from both RAG tools) and user preferences (vote, associated metadata). This data is used to build an open dataset and a public ranking of RAG tools displayed on the platform.

vote.desc: Your votes feed the public ranking of RAG tools and an open dataset the community can reuse to train and evaluate their own systems.

prefs.title: Your preferences

datasets.title: An open dataset

finetune.title: Better RAG tools
finetune.desc: Researchers, product teams and RAG tool authors can use these human preferences to measure the real quality of their pipeline and improve it where it matters.

usage.desc: CompaRAG also serves RAG developers, researchers and trainers looking for concrete comparison data on retrieval pipelines.

explore.title: Explore RAG tools
explore.desc: See the architecture choices (chunker, retriever, reranker) and the real-world performance of each tool in one place.

educate.title: Teach and raise awareness
educate.desc: Use CompaRAG as a teaching aid to compare RAG pipelines and explain their differences to your audience.
